faqs.q: What are forged flanges for heat exchangers used for?
faqs.a: Forged flanges for heat exchangers are used on exchanger nozzles and on large-bore cooling-water and LNG headers. They are made to ASME B16.5 and B16.47 Series A and B, EN 1092-1 and other standards, and built to your data sheet or drawing.

faqs.q: What size range do ASME B16.5 and B16.47 forged flanges cover?
faqs.a: ASME B16.5 covers NPS 1/2–24 (DN 15–600), and large-bore flanges above NPS 24 follow ASME B16.47. Series B covers NPS 26–60 (DN 650–1500). Each unit is made to your drawing, so there is no fixed catalogue size table.

faqs.q: What is the difference between ASME B16.47 Series A and Series B flanges?
faqs.a: Series A has the former MSS SP-44 dimensions and Series B has the former API 605 dimensions, so the two are not interchangeable in Class 150 and 300, nor in NPS 36 and smaller above Class 300. Always state the series when you enquire.

faqs.q: Which standards do forged flanges for heat exchangers follow?
faqs.a: The listing covers ASME B16.5, ASME B16.47 Series A and B, MSS SP-44, EN 1092-1, DIN 2631-2638, GB/T 9112-2010 and JIS B2220. Equivalent grades across standards are indicative only, and we check them against each tender.

faqs.q: Which flange materials can be supplied for exchanger flanges?
faqs.a: Material grades quoted include A105, A350 LF2, A182 and duplex, selected on your data sheet and specification. Each flange ships with its mill certificate and marking to the standard; state the grade, bore and facing on the enquiry.

faqs.q: Are exchanger girth flanges standard B16.5 flanges?
faqs.a: No. Exchanger body and girth flanges are designed with the exchanger and made to its drawing; they are custom-designed, not catalogue B16.5 parts. Girth flange type and the future machining allowance are separate TEMA datasheet fields.

faqs.q: What facing and gasket surface finish apply to flanges on air-cooled exchangers?
faqs.a: Gasket surface finish under ISO 13706 / API 661 is 0.8–1.6 µm Ra (32–64 µin). Ring-type joint facing is available in B16.47 for Class 300–900, NPS 26–36, so state RF or RTJ with the size and pressure class.

faqs.q: What testing and documents come with forged flanges for heat exchangers?
faqs.a: Testing follows the material specification and your NDE requirements, and documentation, inspection and the test plan follow the order’s code and specification. Send your project specification with the enquiry so the quotation includes the right certificates.

faqs.q: Where are forged flanges for heat exchangers used?
faqs.a: They are used as exchanger nozzle and girth flanges for refinery and gas-plant equipment, and as large-bore B16.47 flanges for cooling-water and LNG headers. Tube-side components are on our [tube sheets shelf](/c/tube-sheets) and [baffles and tube supports shelf](/c/baffles-tube-supports).

faqs.q: What do I need to send to quote forged exchanger flanges?
faqs.a: Send the standard and series (B16.5, B16.47 Series A or B, EN 1092-1), the type (weld neck, slip-on, blind, lap joint), facing (RF, RTJ), size and pressure class, material grade, bore or schedule for weld necks, quantity and certification.

faqs.q: Can you supply forged flanges for heat exchangers from Dubai?
faqs.a: Yes. We supply from Dubai, UAE and ship worldwide with the best lead times. These flanges are engineered to your data sheet rather than held as catalogue items, so send the details through [our contact page](/contact) and we quote against them.

faqs.q: Why must the weld neck bore be stated on exchanger flange orders?
faqs.a: For weld necks the bore is matched to the pipe schedule, so the schedule or bore must be on the order. Large-bore flanges above NPS 24 also need the B16.47 series stated, because Series A and B are not interchangeable in most classes.
